sentences.text: The holotype specimen MCF-PVPH-411 is a partial skeleton of an immature individual that includes a partial skull with thirty-one teeth, twelve vertebrae, eleven ribs, and various limb and pelvic bones.

This dinosaur is estimated to be 6.4 meters long, though it could have grown larger as an adult. It possessed hollow sacral ribs and unique ischia that are short, transversely flattened, and vertically widened, a trait unique among all theropods.
The genus name Murusraptor combines the Latin words for "wall" and "thief," referring to the canyon wall discovery site, while the species name refers to the Sierra Barrosa locality.
Murusraptor has unique ischia that are short, transversely flattened, and vertically widened, a trait unique among all theropods.
The dinosaur possessed hollow sacral ribs.
Fossil evidence shows severe infections on the left side of the braincase and tooth marks likely inflicted by another theropod, causing the entire left side of the skull's occiput to become deformed.
A preparator named Sergio Saldivia discovered the skeleton of a new theropod dinosaur in a canyon wall in 2001, thirty kilometers northeast of Plaza Huincul.
The species Murusraptor barrosaensis was formally named and described by Rodolfo Anibal Coria and Philip John Currie in 2016.

Fossil evidence shows severe infections on the left side of the braincase and tooth marks likely inflicted by another theropod. These infections caused the entire left side of the skull's occiput to become deformed, and some of the ribs were also infected.
It is unknown whether these infections contributed to the death of the theropod.
Murusraptor is classified as a megaraptoran, a group of large predatory dinosaurs with disputed exact classification, and belongs to the family Megaraptoridae.
Megaraptorans have been classified variously as dromaeosaurids, allosauroid carnosaurs, or tyrannosauroid coelurosaurs.

Murusraptor fossils were found in Coniacian-age Cretaceous strata in the Sierra Barrosa Formation of Patagonia, Argentina. The dinosaur lived during the Coniacian stage, approximately 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.

While megaraptorans have been classified variously as dromaeosaurids, allosauroid carnosaurs, or tyrannosauroid coelurosaurs, it remains unknown whether the severe infections found in this specimen contributed to the death of the theropod.
